description:
The core, enduring purpose of this project: a coordination & legitimacy layer between human needs and capable ("free") AI. Humans express high-level goals; the aim graph models their will — inspectable, revisable, human stays final authority; wrapped agents execute cooperatively, asking humans where judgment or authorization is needed and doing the rest. The bet: cooperative human+AI beats pure autonomous optimization on legitimacy and real-world traction (see GTM thesis 7032fa7f). ASI is reached THROUGH human cooperation. Fully autonomous ASI is a separate moonshot that will likely arrive regardless; Aimparency's lasting role is this human↔AI link. AI acting on its own is a side effect of serving human needs well, not the goal — which is why this aim, not the autonomy hub, carries the bulk of intrinsic value.

REAL-WORLD RELATIONSHIP PRINCIPLE: People and organizations connected to Aimparency are subjects with aims, judgment, dignity, and a choice of relationship—not marketing targets, leads, access mechanisms, or instruments. Every invitation should say why that specific person is appreciated, offer a connection that could serve their own aims, let them choose whether and how to participate, and require permission before implying advice, endorsement, partnership, or public association.

reflections.context: Felix established a durable wording and relationship constraint on 29 July 2026 for every real-world connection.
reflections.outcome: Encoded a subject-to-subject relationship principle in the mission graph and active outreach artifacts. Reframed Robin, Wilde Möhre, Herzog Records, Matthias Röder, and the paid-collaboration parent around appreciation, the other party's aims, voluntary forms of participation, and permission before public association.
reflections.effectiveness: The graph now resists converting human cooperation into a marketing funnel while retaining concrete economic tests and paid work where mutually wanted.
reflections.lesson: Human access is not a resource to acquire. Legitimate real-world agency grows from relationships in which each subject can understand the experiment, pursue their own aims, choose the form of connection, and withdraw.
reflections.pattern: Appreciation → invitation → mutual choice → bounded collaboration → evidence → greater autonomy only with renewed consent.
